evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic CWF19L1 variants as a novel cause of autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia and atrophy.
evidence.snippet: Our data confirm CWF19L1 as a novel but rare gene causing ARCA.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in CWF19L1 (splice-site, frameshift, and nonsense alleles, as well as damaging missense alleles) abolish or reduce the protein. The normal biological function of the evolutionarily highly conserved CWF19L1 protein is unknown; its name reflects homology to the yeast Cwf19 spliceosome-associated protein (complexed with cdc5), but a specific molecular function has not been established, so none is asserted here.

evidence.snippet: We identified a homozygous mutation at the invariant +1 position (c.964+1G>A) in intron 9 of the CWF19L1 (complexed with cdc5 protein 19-like 1) gene.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic CWF19L1 variants as a novel cause of autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia and atrophy.
evidence.snippet: Exome sequencing of a girl with ARCA from non-consanguineous Dutch parents revealed two pathogenic variants c.37G>C; p.D13H and c.946A>T; p.K316* in CWF19L1, a gene with an unknown function, recently reported to cause ARCA in a Turkish family.
